solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Trial on air quashed as unsound

indicators.note: something quashed is crushed out of shape, so the letters of TRIAL ON AIR lose their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

explanation.surface: A court case about to be broadcast is thrown out as legally unsound.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal surface makes 'quashed' look like a verdict being overturned; here it only scrambles the ten letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsound reasoning is irrational: not grounded in logic.

clue.text: Old-fashioned Queen is not badly spoken

blocks.note: Qu. is a dictionary abbreviation for queen
AIN'T is the nonstandard, 'badly spoken' way of saying 'is not'

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned queen is being praised for her refined speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'is not badly spoken' as a compliment; it is really a definition of the slang contraction AIN'T.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with a warm edge: a quaint thing charms precisely because it belongs to an earlier age.

clue.text: Take responsibility for joint

blocks.note: a verb: to bear a burden, as if carrying it on your back
a noun: the ball-and-socket joint at the top of the arm

explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' sounds like something shared, fitting the idea of responsibility, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a burden is to take responsibility for it, and the shoulder is a ball-and-socket joint.

clue.text: Make an assessment of slightly bigger garment?

blocks.note: a phrasal verb meaning to weigh up or judge
read literally: clothing one step larger on the label

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: a garment one size up is slightly bigger, and the question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: you measure up a person or situation by eye, much as a tailor judges a fit.

clue.text: Bowler, perhaps, with a hard edge played dismissing squad’s tail-ender

indicators.note: the cricket surface makes 'dismissing' sound like getting a batsman out; here it sends the D out of the fodder
what is played is put into action in a new arrangement, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder before the deletion, 9 letters
the last letter of SQUAD, removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler gets an edge off the bat, and the team's last batsman is out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole surface is cricket, so 'Bowler' looks like the player; it is the hat. Take one D out of A HARD EDGE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a hard round felt hat, so it is an example of headgear; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Leaders in jungle adventure viewed askance in foreign island

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Expedition leaders on a jungle trip abroad are looked at with suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' looks like the people heading the adventure; it asks for the leading letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Java is an Indonesian island, foreign from a British point of view.

clue.text: Whiff linked to unrefined town

indicators.note: the two pieces are linked end to end

blocks.note: BO is body odour, an unpleasant whiff
rough = crude, unrefined

explanation.surface: An unpleasant smell is blamed on a crude, unpolished town.
explanation.walkthrough: BO for body odour is a common crossword abbreviation for a whiff or smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough is a town with its own local government.

clue.text: A stiff probe I’m fighting in early trial?

indicators.note: letters fighting each other are thrown about out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: Someone facing a tough interrogation describes it as a fight in a preliminary hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' suggests a courtroom, but the definition is a first ordeal; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A baptism of fire is a hard first experience, originally a soldier's first battle, so an early trial.

clue.text: Interest shown around former partner with bill? Not definite

indicators.note: IN and ACT, joined by 'with', sit around the former partner

blocks.note: being 'in' something shows interest in it, as in 'into'
an ex is a former partner
a bill passed by Parliament becomes an act

explanation.surface: Someone's interest in an ex and an unpaid bill is left vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a payment demand; in Parliament a bill is a draft law, which becomes an Act once passed.
explanation.definitionFit: A near-synonym: a figure that is not definite lacks precision.

clue.text: One at work with striking potential?

definitions.text: One at work with striking potential?

blocks.note: simply an employee, someone with a job
not a hard hitter but someone who can down tools and walk out in an industrial dispute

explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking potential' sounds like a boxer or a match, but a trade unionist can go on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade unionist is a worker in a union, able to strike.

clue.text: Commonplace room for manoeuvre after start of proceedings

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
'after' is a placing word: the letters for room for manoeuvre are written after the P

blocks.note: first letter of PROCEEDINGS
latitude is freedom of action

explanation.surface: At the start of a hearing, someone asks for some room for manoeuvre as a matter of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonplace' reads as an adjective, but here it is the noun: a trite remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a commonplace, a remark used too often to carry meaning.

clue.text: Drive shown by a graduate in play

blocks.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for Drive
as it stands
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate actor shows great drive in a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like ambition; it is the address abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: any play for stage, screen or radio is a drama.

clue.text: Director enthralled by two Latin books of old is a clot

indicators.note: what is enthralled is held captive, so D is held inside

blocks.note: two in Roman numerals
D is a standard abbreviation for director
OT is the Old Testament, the older books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A film director fascinated by ancient Latin texts is dismissed as a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin' is the signal to use Roman numerals, so 'two' becomes a pair of ones with the director between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot is British slang for a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Express disapproval of fall in value? One gets ignored

indicators.note: the ignored one is left out of DEPRECIATE

blocks.note: to depreciate is to fall in value
Roman numeral one, removed

explanation.surface: Someone disapproves of a falling currency, but their complaint is ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are easily confused; dropping one I turns falling in value into disapproving.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: deprecating a practice means openly disapproving of it; the word is often confused with depreciate.

clue.text: An act ally devised around Italy — characterising some thinking?

indicators.note: the fodder goes around the I for Italy
something devised is newly put together, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Diplomats devise a pact with Italy as their ally, which says something about their thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The I for Italy joins the nine letters of AN ACT ALLY before the whole lot is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Analytical thinking breaks a problem into its parts; the question mark admits the loose definition.

clue.text: Fool obstructing secure computer accessory

indicators.note: something obstructing a passage sits in the middle of it

blocks.note: to moor a boat is to secure it
nit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Some idiot is blocking access to a computer peripheral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secure' looks like an adjective describing the accessory; it is the verb MOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the screen plugged into a computer displays its output.

clue.text: Article, one going into most of game following a recurrent idea?

indicators.note: most of MATCH is all but its last letter
a thing going into another enters it, so the one is placed inside the shortened game

blocks.note: the definite article
a match is a game, cut to MATC
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A newspaper article on a sports match develops a recurring theme.
explanation.walkthrough: THE comes first, then MATC with I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thematic means relating to a theme, and a theme is a recurrent idea.

clue.text: Short amateur favoured element in theatre?

blocks.note: curt = short, brusque
A is a standard abbreviation for amateur
in = in favour, fashionable

explanation.surface: A short amateur actor is the favourite for a part in a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of the amateur's height; it means curt.
explanation.definitionFit: The curtain is part of any theatre; the question mark concedes the loose definition.

clue.text: Box secreted by Mexican is terrifying

indicators.note: what is secreted by the words is concealed within them

blocks.note: mexiCAN IS TERrifying

explanation.surface: A frightening Mexican is hiding a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secreted' suggests hiding contraband; it hides the answer across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small round box, often metal, for tea, film or gas.

clue.text: Deceptive image misleading a few lands

indicators.note: misleading letters lead the solver astray from their real order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A mirage deceives travellers crossing a few countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misleading' belongs with 'deceptive' in the surface, which hides that it is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A false dawn is a light before sunrise that fools the eye, and so a hope that proves illusory.

clue.text: Lad working around start of week showing pale colour

indicators.note: working letters are moved about into a new order
the rearranged LAD goes around MON

blocks.note: anagram fodder, becoming AL...D
Mon is the abbreviation for Monday, the start of the week

explanation.surface: A lad at work on a Monday morning looks pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of week' tempts you to take just W; here it is MON, the day that starts the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Almond is a pale creamy yellow-brown shade.

clue.text: Authority for example supplied by note

blocks.note: say = for instance
so (soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An official's authority is backed up by a written note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a memo; it is a musical note in do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: acting on someone's word alone means relying on their authority.

clue.text: Approval during endless shopping outlay is uttered

indicators.note: OK comes during, so inside, the outlay
endless SPEND loses its last letter

blocks.note: a shopper's spend is their outlay, cut to SPEN
an OK is approval

explanation.surface: Someone voices approval throughout a never-ending shopping spree.
explanation.walkthrough: SPEN is split around OK: SP-OK-EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken means uttered aloud in words.

clue.text: Country not out to get revolutionary support

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so AID turns round

blocks.note: in cricket a batsman not out is still in
aid = support, becoming DIA

explanation.surface: A nation stays in power to win backing from rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks political; it only turns AID round.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the South Asian republic is one country among many.

clue.text: Raised platform is supporting US lawyer

indicators.note: in a down answer, what supports something sits below it, so IS follows DA

blocks.note: a District Attorney, an American public prosecutor
as it stands

explanation.surface: A raised stage holds up an American lawyer making a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives IS first, but 'supporting' in a down clue puts it underneath DA.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the platform at the end of a hall for speakers or a high table.

clue.text: New-fangled limos in US for despotic figure

indicators.note: new-fangled things are made in a new form, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A dictator is driven around America in modern limousines.
explanation.walkthrough: Stretch limos for a despot sound plausible, but the letters themselves are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Benito Mussolini was the Fascist dictator of Italy.

clue.text: Rebel’s work, rejecting society in form of book

indicators.note: the rejected S is thrown out of SEDITION

blocks.note: sedition is the work of a rebel, stirring revolt
S is the standard abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A rebel's manifesto that rejects society is published as a book.
explanation.walkthrough: SEDITION loses its S to leave EDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is one form in which a book is published, such as a paperback or revised edition.

clue.text: Polished English cricket side followed by six-footer

indicators.note: ANT follows the English cricket side

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the side the batsman stands on
an ant has six legs

explanation.surface: A refined English cricket team is followed onto the field by a very tall player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is any insect, here the ant. 'Cricket side' is a team in the surface but the leg side of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished and elegant both mean refined and stylish.
